A0020.title: Account Penalty
A0020.definition: Penalizing accounts when they violate related rules, and prohibiting related behaviors or actions.
A0020.description: Identity punishment strategies are an effective means of restricting illegitimate or non-compliant users from causing persistent damage to the business. Identity punishment can operate at two levels: first, restrictions on the account itself, such as temporary suspension, warning notices, or revocation of authorization; second, restrictions on the resources the account can access, such as disabling specific business functions, limiting resource usage frequency, deleting resources, or restricting access to illegal resources.
A0020.limitation: Account punishment is a post-event mitigation measure. Attackers often complete activities such as coupon abuse or traffic farming before being penalized, meaning losses have already occurred. Malicious actors can continuously evade punishment by registering new accounts in bulk or appealing bans, and bulk punishment may also inadvertently affect small-scale operations of legitimate users.

A0020-001.title: Store Penalty
A0020-001.definition: Penalizing a store when it violates related rules, and prohibiting related behaviors or actions.
A0020-001.description: Store penalty strategies include: lowering credit ratings, reducing store levels, delisting products, decreasing search weight, suspending stores, banning stores, imposing fines, etc.
A0020-001.limitation: Store penalties are post-event loss prevention measures. Profits from violations such as fake orders and fraudulent transactions are often already realized before the store is demoted or banned, making losses difficult to recover. Malicious merchants can bypass penalties by re-registering stores under new identities or using other entities. Improper calibration of demotion and banning severity can also easily harm normal small and medium-sized merchants.

A0020-002.title: Employee Penalty
A0020-002.definition: Employee penalty strategies are a set of sanctions established by an organization in response to employees violating company rules or policies.
A0020-002.description: Penalty content may include verbal warnings, written warnings, suspension, demotion, salary deductions, termination, etc. Effective employee penalty strategies should balance punishment and improvement, making employees aware of the consequences of misconduct while providing opportunities for correction and improvement.
A0020-002.limitation: Limitations include the potential to cause employee dissatisfaction and affect the work environment. Compliance must be ensured to guard against legal action. Therefore, fair, clear, and consistently enforced strategies must be developed in alignment with relevant regulations and company policies.

A0020-003.title: Account Ban
A0020-003.definition: Banning an account when it violates related rules, preventing the account from logging in.
A0020-003.description: Account banning policies involve prohibiting account login when accounts violate relevant rules. These policies include account banning, account freezing, account cancellation, and account destruction. Bans can be classified by duration into temporary bans and permanent bans, and by scope into single-service bans and platform-wide bans. They are often combined with dimensions such as device fingerprints and IP addresses to impose joint penalties on associated accounts, thereby increasing the cost of account replacement for illicit actors.
A0020-003.limitation: Account banning is a post-incident mitigation measure. Attackers often complete activities such as reward abuse, fraud, or traffic manipulation before being banned, meaning losses have already occurred. Illicit actors can continuously circumvent bans through bulk registration of new accounts, changing device fingerprints, or appealing for unbanning. Additionally, mass banning may inadvertently affect legitimate users who share devices or IP addresses.
